CHAPTER XIII
CRIMINAL SANCTIONS
Article 63
Every person or institution that commits acts resulting in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, coercion, or deprivation of liberty against women and children such that a violation of this regional regulation occurs, shall be subject to criminal sanctions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: Region is Tanah Toraja Regency. Regent is the Regent of Tana Toraja. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the regional house of representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administrator. Sub-district is a part of the regency area that is led by a sub-district head. Lembang is another term for village which is part of the regency area that is led by the Head of Lembang; Lembang Government is the term used for the village government in Tana Toraja Regency. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife and their children, or father and children or mother and children or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward laterally to the third degree. Parents are biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. Guardian is a person or entity that in reality exercises custodial power as a parent over a child. Woman is a human being who can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth and breastfeed. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a baby still in the womb. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. Protection of women is all efforts made to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. Empowerment of women is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. Adopted Child is a Child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the Family of Parents, legal Guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of that Child into the environment of the adoptive Parents' Family based on a court decision or determination. Foster Child is a Child who is cared for by a person or institution to be provided with guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health because the Parents or one of the Parents is unable to guarantee the proper growth and development of the Child. Custody is the power of Parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the Child in accordance with the religion professed and in accordance with the ability, talent, and interest. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. Assistant is a social worker who has professional competence in their field. Violence is any act that is against the law, which results in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a cooperative network that carries out integrated social service functions. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a cooperative network that carries out integrated service functions for the protection of women and children. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations. Family Welfare Consultation Institution hereinafter abbreviated as LK3 is an integrated social service unit that implements psychosocial problem handling for families to realize family resilience. Regional Child Protection Commission hereinafter abbreviated as KPAD is an integrated social service unit that implements child protection services to realize the fulfillment of children's rights.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANA TORAJA REGENCY
NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are creations of God who possess dignity and honor as well as human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to receive the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity and honor of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy household life, society, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while simultaneously providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in efforts to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to assign responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

Article 50
The obligations and responsibilities of parents and family as referred to in Article 45 letter d, are to safeguard and prevent the occurrence of all forms of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination both against women and against children.
The obligations and responsibilities of parents towards children as referred to in paragraph (1), are to:
1. care for, maintain, educate, and protect children;
2. develop children in accordance with their abilities, talents, and interests;
3. prevent the occurrence of marriage at the age of a child (child marriage); and
4. provide character education and instill moral values in children.
Guardians and/or foster parents who have obtained a determination as referred to in Article 46 paragraph (3), must be able to fulfill the provisions as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (2) letter a.
Guardians and/or foster parents who are appointed as referred to in paragraph (3) must have the same religion as that professed by the Child.
Guardians and/or foster parents as referred to in paragraph (3) are responsible for the child and are obligated to manage the property belonging to the child concerned for the best interests of the child.
Guardians and/or foster parents as referred to in paragraph (3), may represent the child to perform legal acts, both inside and outside the court for the best interests of the child.

Article 41
The Regional Government provides special protection for children who are economically and/or sexually exploited as referred to in Article 37 letter d and children who are victims of violence, both physical and mental, as referred to in Article 37 letter h.
Special protection for exploited children and children who are victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. dissemination of laws and regulations related to the protection of children who are economically and/or sexually exploited;
b. monitoring, reporting, and the imposition of sanctions; and
c. involvement of various organizations, the Regional Government, companies, labor unions, social institutions, and the community.

Article 47
In order to implement the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 46 paragraph (1), the Regent shall establish programs and action activities for the protection of women and children in the regional action plan as a basis for regional apparatus in implementing the protection of women and children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.
The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1), constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).
Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by the Regent's Regulation.

Fourth Part
Protection of Women

Article 34
Protection in the field of education as referred to in Article 30 paragraph (1), applies both outside the school environment and within the school environment.
Protection outside the school environment is safeguarding and preventing a child from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.
Protection within the school environment is protection from acts of violence that can be committed either by school administrators, by teachers, or by their own friends.

Paragraph 1
Prevention of Violence

Article 21
Every child who becomes a perpetrator or victim of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are creations of God who possess dignity and honor as well as human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to receive the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity and honor of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy household life, society, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while simultaneously providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in efforts to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to assign responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

Article 41
The Regional Government provides special protection for children who are economically and/or sexually exploited as referred to in Article 37 letter d and children who are victims of violence, both physical and mental, as referred to in Article 37 letter h.
Special protection for exploited children and children who are victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. dissemination of laws and regulations related to the protection of children who are economically and/or sexually exploited;
b. monitoring, reporting, and the imposition of sanctions; and
c. involvement of various organizations, the Regional Government, companies, labor unions, social institutions, and the community.

Article 8
In order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize equality and gender justice in family life, community life, national life, and state life, women must be empowered.
The empowerment of women as referred to in paragraph (1) is directed to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in activities:
a. economic;
b. socio-cultural;
c. political; and
d. legal.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANA TORAJA REGENCY
NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are creations of God who possess dignity and honor as well as human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to receive the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity and honor of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy household life, society, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while simultaneously providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in efforts to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to assign responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANA TORAJA REGENCY
NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are creations of God who possess dignity and honor as well as human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to receive the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity and honor of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy household life, society, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while simultaneously providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in efforts to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to assign responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

Article 50
The obligations and responsibilities of parents and family as referred to in Article 45 letter d, are to safeguard and prevent the occurrence of all forms of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination both against women and against children.
The obligations and responsibilities of parents towards children as referred to in paragraph (1), are to:
1. care for, maintain, educate, and protect children;
2. develop children in accordance with their abilities, talents, and interests;
3. prevent the occurrence of marriage at the age of a child (child marriage); and
4. provide character education and instill moral values in children.
Guardians and/or foster parents who have obtained a determination as referred to in Article 46 paragraph (3), must be able to fulfill the provisions as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (2) letter a.
Guardians and/or foster parents who are appointed as referred to in paragraph (3) must have the same religion as that professed by the Child.
Guardians and/or foster parents as referred to in paragraph (3) are responsible for the child and are obligated to manage the property belonging to the child concerned for the best interests of the child.
Guardians and/or foster parents as referred to in paragraph (3), may represent the child to perform legal acts, both inside and outside the court for the best interests of the child.

Article 41
The Regional Government provides special protection for children who are economically and/or sexually exploited as referred to in Article 37 letter d and children who are victims of violence, both physical and mental, as referred to in Article 37 letter h.
Special protection for exploited children and children who are victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. dissemination of laws and regulations related to the protection of children who are economically and/or sexually exploited;
b. monitoring, reporting, and the imposition of sanctions; and
c. involvement of various organizations, the Regional Government, companies, labor unions, social institutions, and the community.

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are creations of God who possess dignity and honor as well as human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to receive the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity and honor of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy household life, society, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while simultaneously providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in efforts to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to assign responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANA TORAJA REGENCY
NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are creations of God who possess dignity and honor as well as human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to receive the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity and honor of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy household life, society, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while simultaneously providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in efforts to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to assign responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

Guardians and/or foster parents as referred to in paragraph (3), may represent the child to perform legal acts, both inside and outside the court for the best interests of the child.

Article 34
Protection in the field of education as referred to in Article 30 paragraph (1), applies both outside the school environment and within the school environment.
Protection outside the school environment is safeguarding and preventing a child from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.
Protection within the school environment is protection from acts of violence that can be committed either by school administrators, by teachers, or by their own friends.

Article 19
Every child has the right to obtain protection from being a target of persecution, torture, or the imposition of inhumane punishment.
Every child has the right to obtain liberty in accordance with the law.
Every child has the right to be protected from arrest and detention, and/or juvenile imprisonment shall only be carried out if in accordance with applicable law and can only be carried out as a last resort.

Article 47
In order to implement the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 46 paragraph (1), the Regent shall establish programs and action activities for the protection of women and children in the regional action plan as a basis for regional apparatus in implementing the protection of women and children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.
The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1), constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).
Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by the Regent's Regulation.

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are creations of God who possess dignity and honor as well as human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to receive the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity and honor of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy household life, society, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while simultaneously providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in efforts to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to assign responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANA TORAJA REGENCY
NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are creations of God who possess dignity and honor as well as human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to receive the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity and honor of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy household life, society, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while simultaneously providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in efforts to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to assign responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

Paragraph 1
Prevention of Violence

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANA TORAJA REGENCY
NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are creations of God who possess dignity and honor as well as human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to receive the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity and honor of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy household life, society, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while simultaneously providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in efforts to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to assign responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are creations of God who possess dignity and honor as well as human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to receive the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity and honor of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy household life, society, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while simultaneously providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in efforts to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to assign responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

Article 50

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANA TORAJA REGENCY
NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are creations of God who possess dignity and honor as well as human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to receive the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity and honor of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy household life, society, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while simultaneously providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in efforts to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to assign responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are creations of God who possess dignity and honor as well as human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to receive the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity and honor of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy household life, society, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while simultaneously providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in efforts to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to assign responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are creations of God who possess dignity and honor as well as human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to receive the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity and honor of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy household life, society, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while simultaneously providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in efforts to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to assign responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

Article 41

a. dissemination of laws and regulations related to the protection of children who are economically and/or sexually exploited;
b. monitoring, reporting, and the imposition of sanctions; and
c. involvement of various organizations, the Regional Government, companies, labor unions, social institutions, and the community.

Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife and their children, or father and children or mother and children or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward laterally to the third degree. OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANA TORAJA REGENCY
NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are creations of God who possess dignity and honor as well as human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to receive the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity and honor of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy household life, society, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while simultaneously providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in efforts to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to assign responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

Article 50
The obligations and responsibilities of parents and family as referred to in Article 45 letter d, are to safeguard and prevent the occurrence of all forms of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination both against women and against children.
The obligations and responsibilities of parents towards children as referred to in paragraph (1), are to:
1. care for, maintain, educate, and protect children;
2. develop children in accordance with their abilities, talents, and interests;
3. prevent the occurrence of marriage at the age of a child (child marriage); and
4. provide character education and instill moral values in children.
Guardians and/or foster parents who have obtained a determination as referred to in Article 46 paragraph (3), must be able to fulfill the provisions as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (2) letter a.
Guardians and/or foster parents who are appointed as referred to in paragraph (3) must have the same religion as that professed by the Child.
Guardians and/or foster parents as referred to in paragraph (3) are responsible for the child and are obligated to manage the property belonging to the child concerned for the best interests of the child.
Guardians and/or foster parents as referred to in paragraph (3), may represent the child to perform legal acts, both inside and outside the court for the best interests of the child.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANA TORAJA REGENCY
NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are creations of God who possess dignity and honor as well as human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to receive the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity and honor of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy household life, society, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while simultaneously providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in efforts to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to assign responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANA TORAJA REGENCY
NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are creations of God who possess dignity and honor as well as human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to receive the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity and honor of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy household life, society, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while simultaneously providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in efforts to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to assign responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANA TORAJA REGENCY
NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are creations of God who possess dignity and honor as well as human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to receive the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity and honor of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy household life, society, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while simultaneously providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in efforts to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to assign responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: Region is Tanah Toraja Regency. Regent is the Regent of Tana Toraja. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the regional house of representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administrator. Sub-district is a part of the regency area that is led by a sub-district head. Lembang is another term for village which is part of the regency area that is led by the Head of Lembang; Lembang Government is the term used for the village government in Tana Toraja Regency. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife and their children, or father and children or mother and children or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward laterally to the third degree. Parents are biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. Guardian is a person or entity that in reality exercises custodial power as a parent over a child. Woman is a human being who can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth and breastfeed. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a baby still in the womb. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. Protection of women is all efforts made to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. Empowerment of women is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. Adopted Child is a Child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the Family of Parents, legal Guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of that Child into the environment of the adoptive Parents' Family based on a court decision or determination. Foster Child is a Child who is cared for by a person or institution to be provided with guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health because the Parents or one of the Parents is unable to guarantee the proper growth and development of the Child. Custody is the power of Parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the Child in accordance with the religion professed and in accordance with the ability, talent, and interest. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. Assistant is a social worker who has professional competence in their field. Violence is any act that is against the law, which results in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a cooperative network that carries out integrated social service functions. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a cooperative network that carries out integrated service functions for the protection of women and children. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations. Family Welfare Consultation Institution hereinafter abbreviated as LK3 is an integrated social service unit that implements psychosocial problem handling for families to realize family resilience. Regional Child Protection Commission hereinafter abbreviated as KPAD is an integrated social service unit that implements child protection services to realize the fulfillment of children's rights.

Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields, and other aspects of life.
